title: Bootstrap AutoTour as a cross-agent installable package

fields.outcome: Package maintainers can initialize, install, validate, and extend AutoTour from a clean Git repository across Claude, Codex, Cursor, and portable Agent Plugin hosts.
fields.scope: Initialize Git on main; add an MIT-licensed npm package scaffold, portable and compatibility plugin metadata, a reusable AutoTour skill, a minimal CLI, a modular walkthrough schema, tests, and CI. Browser capture, DOM replay, rendering, and dependency tracing are excluded from this bootstrap.
fields.acceptance: Git identity, npm packing and installation, agent metadata, project initialization, the walkthrough contract, and automated verification behave as the criteria specify.
fields.decisions: Use Node.js ESM and the unscoped npm name autotour, which was unclaimed when checked. Treat root plugin.json and skills/ as canonical portable metadata, with Codex, Claude, and Cursor compatibility files. Keep credentials out of committed JSON and local output ignored.
fields.verification: Run the Node test suite, package validation, npm pack dry-run, CLI smoke checks, plugin manifest validation, AgentHouse frozen evaluation, and Git housekeeping inspection.
fields.dependencies: Node.js 20 or newer, Playwright 1.63, Ajv 8.20, and Ajv Formats 3.0.
fields.risks: The unclaimed npm name is not reserved until publication. Host plugin formats can evolve. Browser capture and rendering remain future work and are stated as unavailable in the README.

criteria.expectation: The repository uses main and has local author metadata for Valerio Neri without changing global Git settings.
npm can pack an MIT-licensed public package named autotour with a working autotour executable.
The package contains valid portable, Codex, Claude, and Cursor discovery metadata plus at least one usable skill.
autotour init creates a repository-managed JSON configuration without storing credentials.
A published JSON Schema describes modular walkthroughs, outputs, publication choices, and source dependencies.
Automated tests and CI verify CLI behavior, metadata consistency, schema samples, and package contents.
